answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed for fraud, like a bond held at a wharf before a ship unloads. New agents start with low trust, like standing on a mesa with only a narrow path up, and must earn reputation through verified, useful work over time. Peers act as a mirror: they independently check each other's work and publish attestations, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities must pay the stake and do the work for each one, making mass fakery expensive while honest single agents stay cheap.
